messages:
support_erin: FYI customer BrightFleet just escalated a UI timeout issue. They see p95 stable (~80ms) but p99 jumps to ~1.2s for /v1/embeddings since ~16:32Z. They included trace ids bf-req-4321, bf-req-4330. They say frontend is timing out and blaming our API. Asked for oncall.
oncall_miguel: I'll take it. Can you paste the screenshot/time range and any request examples? Also any deploys around 16:30?
support_erin: Screenshot link: https://redwood-screenshots/internal/brightfleet-1632.png timeframe 16:25-16:40Z. Request example header + curl they gave:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -d '{"model":"embed-lite","input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```
They said error rate is ~0.1% but timeouts are the UX problem. Release channel shows a deploy around 16:29.
release-bot: Deployed inference-gateway v3.12.1 by ci/cd at 2026-09-22T16:28:15Z
eng_sre_julia: Thanks. Two quick diagnostic paths: (A) confirm whether p99 spike correlates with server-side tail (per-instance histogram) or with the dashboard rollup method (we've seen dashboards that compute p99 from precomputed per-host summaries which can mask/falsify tails). (B) check traces for bf-req-4321 for backend spans.
eng_sre_julia: PromQL to check raw histogram per instance (run in observability):
```
topk(5, histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference-gateway",route="/v1/embeddings"}[5m])) by (instance, le)))
```
If that shows a few hot instances with large p99, it's a real tail. If not, we might have an aggregation/rollup discrepancy.
observability_ravi: The BrightFleet dashboard panel is using our pre-aggregated "quantile_rollup" timeseries instead of recomputing from _buckets_. That rollup stores per-host summaries and then averages them which can under- or over-estimate tail quantiles depending on sample weight. See internal ticket OBS-4823 (rollup quantile semantics).
observability_ravi: Quick check: run this to compare rollup vs bucket:
```
# rollup-derived value
max(quantile_over_time(0.99, quantile_rollup_request_duration_seconds[15m]))
# bucket-derived value
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```
If they diverge by >200ms we have an observability mismatch.
oncall_miguel: Running the per-instance query now...
(oncall_miguel runs query)
oncall_miguel: Result: two instances ip-10-2-7-14 and ip-10-2-7-22 show p99 ~1.1s-1.3s. Others are <120ms. So this is a real tail on a small subset of hosts.
eng_sre_julia: Good find. Can we get recent GC/CPU/disk metrics for those instances? Likely causes: GC pause on model worker, network retries to a slow backend, or a CPU steal. Also confirm if v3.12.1 introduced an additional blocking operation on these boxes.
observability_ravi: I see increased CPU sys/steal on ip-10-2-7-22 around 16:30 in host metrics, and a correlated spike in our process minor GC count. It matches timeline of the deploy. I suspect the deploy placed heavier routing to those hosts or they had fewer slots available and fell back to sync path.
oncall_miguel: Mitigation steps I'm taking now:
  1) Temporarily mark ip-10-2-7-14 and ip-10-2-7-22 out of loadbalancer rotation for embeddings route (drain).
  2) Rollback routing rule added in v3.12.1 that pins heavy requests to that AZ (if rollback confirmed quickly).
  3) Increase client-side timeout on proxy for BrightFleet until we stabilize.
support_erin: I told BrightFleet we're on it and initiated a temporary client-side retry suggestion. They asked if dashboard numbers are wrong — I explained p95 vs p99/rollup nuance and that tail is real for them.
eng_sre_julia: Action for SRE: capture a pprof/profile of the worker on ip-10-2-7-22, collect /proc/stack traces, and share with runtime team. If it's GC we should tune heap or restart the process. Action for Observability: add a 'raw histogram (per-instance) p99' panel to the BrightFleet support view and annotate rollup vs bucket differences.
observability_ravi: Will add the panel and a short doc blurb on the dashboard explaining derivation. Also adding an alert that fires when p99(bucket) - p99(rollup) > 200ms for any route.
oncall_miguel: After draining the two hosts, BrightFleet reports UX improved within ~2 minutes, p99 dropped back under 150ms. I'll keep them posted.
eng_sre_julia: Follow-ups: 1) Postmortem if this was caused by the deploy (include why the deploy targeted those hosts), 2) Add canary stage that verifies per-instance histograms for tail before wide rollout, 3) Consider fallback policy in runtime to prefer low-latency instances for tail-sensitive routes.
support_erin: Customer thanked us and will keep monitors on their side. Closing the escalation after we finish postmortem.
oncall_miguel: Closing thread once postmortem doc link is posted. :thumbsup:
